mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 2% risk-free rate benchmark during inflation spikes above 0.3%, or the SPX 20-day return is negative when CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index (>2% month-over-month for two consecutive months) coincides with increased corporate hiring intentions, elevating expected future profits and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor cost increases, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or corporate hiring intentions (from NFP proxies) show no correlation with SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index (<90 for two consecutive months) indicates weakening industrial production capacity, which reduces upward price pressure and increases equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 90 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During INDPRO contraction periods, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or INDPRO recovers quickly and SPX returns positively within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST retail sales index (>5% MoM) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in RSAFS used car sales (>3% MoM) signals a shift toward consumer durable demand, which elevates growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases >5% MoM AND RSAFS decreases >3% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: During such dual signals, SPX 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10), or the effect persists for less than 3 days.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for three consecutive months, the anticipation of higher borrowing costs suppresses equity risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During high-rate periods, SPX 20-day returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.05 over 6 months), or FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for the next 6 months with SPX returns neutral.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 4% (4 consecutive months) reflects labor market slack, reducing wage growth expectations and compressing equity valuations, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During UNRATE < 4% periods, SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or UNRATE re-enters >4% within 3 months and SPX returns turn positive.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in INDPRO (first falling below 100, then rising back above but remaining below 105 for two months) indicates persistent supply-side imbalances, which amplifies uncertainty and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 AND INDPRO > 100 but < 105 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such INDPRO patterns, SPX 20-day returns are not negative (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent when other supply indicators (e.g., GDPC1) show no abnormality.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly acceleration in both GDPC1 (demand) and a deceleration in RSAFS (discretionary spending) by at least 2% MoM each suggests a structural shift toward consumption-led growth, which elevates equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% MoM AND RSAFS decreases by >2% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: During such dual signals, SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent when other demand proxies (e.g., HOUST) do not confirm the pattern.
